title: Atomic manifest canonicalization and signed release pipeline for model onboarding
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Implement a CI/CD pipeline that produces canonical, deterministic model+profile manifests, cryptographically signs artifacts using delegated signing keys, and publishes an atomic release bundle with sequence numbers so consumers (hosted, dedicated, private) can pin reliably. The pipeline must support staged traffic, safe rollbacks, and automated verification steps (repro build, perf sanity, signature validation) before promotion to public channels.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline generates a canonical manifest (JSON-LD) that is bit-for-bit reproducible from inputs and build metadata
Build artifacts are signed with a rotating, auditable signing key; signature and key metadata are included in the manifest
Publish operation is atomic: consumers see either old or new bundle (sequence ordinal) and can pin to an exact manifest key
Automated canary promotion flow: blue/green markers and traffic tags are emitted to rollout controller after successful smoke/perf checks
Rollbacks can be performed by promoting previous manifest sequence without requiring re-signing
Audit trail links (CI run, PR, attestations) are embedded in the manifest and surfaced in Console release UI
Security review checklist completed and KMS/HSM integration verified with ops
End-to-end smoke test passes for hosted API and dedicated instance using published profile and model artifact
tasks: Design canonical manifest schema and deterministic serialization rules (sort keys, normalize timestamps, embed reproducible provenance)
Extend build pipeline to emit reproducible build bundle (binaries, quantized weights, perf profile) and a hash manifest
Integrate Cosign-equivalent signing step wired to our delegated KMS signing key with rotation metadata
Implement atomic publish service that writes bundle to artifact storage under monotonically increasing sequence IDs and updates release index in a single transactional step
Add CI gates: reproducible build verification, perf regression check against baseline, signature validation
Wire Console to display manifest sequence, attestation links, and allow pinning to a manifest key
Create canary promotion job: traffic markers for rollout-controller and telemetry hooks to collect early signals
Add runbooks for key compromise, failed promotion, and emergency rollback
comments: 2025-03-05 - Aisha Rao: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Confluence. Agreed on deterministic serialization (lexicographic key sorting, ISO-8601 zeroed fractional seconds) and embedding provenance with source repo/commit/build-id.

2025-03-08 - Marco Diaz: PoC for canonicalizer completed. PoC repo: github.com/redwood-inference/canonicalizer (branch ENG-81207-poc). Observed non-determinism in tar ordering; switched to deterministic zstd bundle without mtime metadata.

2025-03-10 - Security (Priya Menon): Reviewed signing approach. Recommend use of HSM-backed delegated signing key with 1-week rotation window and retained key IDs in manifest. Flagged requirement for offline key emergency rotation runbook.

2025-03-12 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Atomic publish needs advisory for storage semantics. We'll leverage conditional writes to the release-index table and a storage object prefix using sequence numbers to provide atomicity.

2025-03-15 - Marco Diaz: Implemented Cosign-style signatures and included a 'manifest_sequence' field. CI gate added to reject manifest if signature missing or verification fails. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/release-pipeline/pull/324
2025-03-18 - PM (Noelle Park): UX story for Console is drafted. Console should show 'pinned by customer' hint and allow manual rollback to a previous sequence. Link: Confluence UX attachment.

2025-03-20 - Aisha Rao: Began wiring canary promotion job; collecting telemetry schema for early quality signals. Created runbook drafts for rollback and key compromise scenarios. Next: complete integration tests with hosted and dedicated smoke harnesses.
